cues.text: Watch as F1 Finance's audit machine looks for bills missing from the books.
It reads the payments made after year end. A $186,400 bill for June work is missing.
Unpaid bills too: a $23,480 legal bill for May and June is missing.
Four late June bills missed the year.
An accrual books a cost in its own month. June's interest, $28,665, was never accrued.
Last, it adds up what it found against materiality, the size of mistake that matters, and writes the workpapers for the CPA.

All done. The missing bills add up to almost $248,000, just under the auditors' working limit, so the CPA weighs them with the rest of the audit. Eight items stay open. The CPA, a person, concludes and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
